An event study: the effect period by period around adoption

Source: R/evtst.R
evtst.Rd

Leads and lags of a policy's adoption from a two-way fixed-effects regression on indicators of the time since adoption, with the joint test that the leads are zero (no effect before the policy, the testable part of parallel trends), and the raw mean outcome of each adoption cohort around its adoption.

Usage

evtst(
  y,
  unit,
  time,
  first,
  leads = 4,
  lags = 4,
  ref = -1,
  bin = TRUE,
  adj = NULL,
  clus = NULL,
  w = NULL,
  ma = 1,
  norm = TRUE,
  mbar = NULL,
  target = NULL,
  draws = 5000,
  seed = NULL,
  level = 0.95
)

Arguments

y

The outcome: finite numbers, one per row (counts from 0 for fam = "pois" or "nb").

unit

The unit of each row: labels.

time

The period of each row: whole numbers (a year, a month counted from a start); each unit at most once per period.

first

The period each row's unit is first treated: numbers, constant within units; NA, 0 or Inf for a unit never treated. Treatment is taken to stay on.

leads, lags

The periods before and after adoption estimated: whole numbers, leads at least 1 and lags at least 0.

ref

The event time left out: a whole number from -leads to lags.

bin

TRUE to bin event times beyond the window into its ends, FALSE to drop their rows.

adj

NULL or time-varying controls: a data frame or list of columns, a numeric matrix, or one vector, one value per row. Factor, text and logical columns enter as indicators of each level but the first.

clus

NULL (cluster by unit), the cluster of each row (labels), or a list or data frame of two such columns for two-way clustering.

w

NULL or weights from 0, one per row (population, matching weights); rows of weight 0 take no part.

ma

The width of the moving average of the cohort means: a whole number, at least 1 (1 for none).

norm

TRUE to scale each cohort's means to 1 in the period before adoption.

mbar

NULL, or the bounds on the departure from parallel trends relative to the largest before adoption: numbers from 0.

target

NULL for the mean effect after adoption, or one event time from 0.

draws

The normal draws of the sensitivity interval: a whole number from 100.

seed

The seed of the draws: NULL to draw it from R's generator, or a whole number from 0.

level

The confidence level of the intervals: one number strictly between 0 and 1.

Value

An object of class evtst, a list: est, one row per event time (evtm, est, se, lo, hi, stat, p), the reference a row with est 0; pre, the pre-trend test (f, df1, df2, p; NA without leads to test); vcov, the variance of the estimated event times; coh, the cohort means (cohort, evtm, value); n, the rows used; ncl, the clusters; and level; with mbar, sens (mbar, lob, upb, lo, hi) and brk, else NULL.

Details

With G_i the period unit i is first treated and k = t - G_i, the model is y_it = sum_k g_k 1(t - G_i = k) + adj_it'th + a_i + m_t + e_it for k from -leads to lags but ref, the period left out (the one before adoption by default). Times beyond the window are binned into its ends (bin = TRUE) or their rows dropped. Units never treated have every indicator 0. The variance, the clusters and the degrees of freedom are those of didfe(). The pre-trend test is the Wald statistic W = g_pre' V_pre^-1 g_pre over the leads, reported as F = W / q on q and G - 1 degrees of freedom.

With staggered adoption and effects that change over time, the lead and lag coefficients can mix in effects from other periods (Sun and Abraham 2021); stgdid() gives event-time effects free of that.

coh is the mean outcome of each cohort (the units first treated in one period) in each period, as a trailing moving average over ma periods, by time since adoption within the window, and with norm = TRUE scaled to 1 in the period before adoption: a check, before any model, that the cohorts moved together before the policy.

With mbar, the effects are bounded when the trend after adoption may depart from parallel by up to mbar times the largest departure seen before it (the relative magnitudes of Rambachan and Roth 2023): with D the largest change between consecutive pre-period coefficients (the reference at 0), the bias at event time e >= 0 is at most (e + 1) mbar D, so the identified set of the target (the mean effect after adoption, or the event time target) is its estimate +- the mean of (e + 1) times mbar D (lob, upb). The interval (lo, hi) draws the coefficients draws times from their normal distribution with the cluster-robust covariance, computes the bounds for each, and takes the (1 - level) / 2 quantile of the lower and the (1 + level) / 2 quantile of the upper: by Bonferroni it covers the identified set with probability at least level. It is conservative; the conditional and hybrid intervals of Rambachan and Roth are shorter. brk is the smallest mbar (by bisection, up to 10; Inf beyond) whose interval holds 0.

References

Sun, L. and Abraham, S. (2021). Estimating dynamic treatment effects in event studies with heterogeneous treatment effects. Journal of Econometrics, 225(2), 175-199. doi:10.1016/j.jeconom.2020.09.006

Freyaldenhoven, S., Hansen, C. and Shapiro, J. M. (2019). Pre-event trends in the panel event-study design. American Economic Review, 109(9), 3307-3338. doi:10.1257/aer.20180609

Examples

d <- expand.grid(year = 2015:2024, town = LETTERS[1:12])
i <- match(d$town, LETTERS)
d$first <- c(2019, 2019, 2019, 2019, 2021, 2021, 2021, 2021,
             NA, NA, NA, NA)[i]
on <- !is.na(d$first) & d$year >= d$first
d$rate <- 30 + i + 0.5 * (d$year - 2015) - 4 * on + sin(seq_len(120))
e <- evtst(d$rate, d$town, d$year, d$first, leads = 3, lags = 3)
e
#> evtst: 120 rows, 12 clusters
#>  evtm         est        se         lo         hi        stat            p
#>    -3 -0.09567324 0.5231309 -1.2470766  1.0557301  -0.1828859 8.582148e-01
#>    -2  0.05394300 0.3573220 -0.7325173  0.8404033   0.1509647 8.827364e-01
#>    -1  0.00000000        NA         NA         NA          NA           NA
#>     0 -4.13423655 0.2277190 -4.6354427 -3.6330304 -18.1549928 1.505547e-09
#>     1 -4.25980824 0.4295541 -5.2052505 -3.3143660  -9.9168141 8.036081e-07
#>     2 -4.29625671 0.6385691 -5.7017379 -2.8907756  -6.7279431 3.251955e-05
#>     3 -4.13228464 0.4571512 -5.1384677 -3.1261016  -9.0392074 2.008834e-06
#> leads jointly zero: F = 0.07293073 on 2 and 11 df, p = 0.9301109
e$pre
#>            f df1 df2         p
#> 1 0.07293073   2  11 0.9301109
# how far trends may bend before the effect is lost
evtst(d$rate, d$town, d$year, d$first, leads = 3, lags = 3,
      mbar = c(0, 1, 2), seed = 1)$sens
#>   mbar       lob       upb        lo         hi
#> 1    0 -4.205647 -4.205647 -4.930333 -3.4716191
#> 2    1 -4.579687 -3.831606 -7.339214 -1.5703317
#> 3    2 -4.953728 -3.457565 -9.831768  0.8305316
